I’ll read the frozen candidate’s review and original board analysis, then build and test an isolated fix under `read-error-fix`. I’ll leave v1 untouched and capture the old failure separately from the corrected recovery results.

The review identifies three required fixes: invalidate cached data and position after a failed read, release any retained window before `freopen` rebinds the stream, and preserve the real errno through public `fflush`.

I’ll keep failed-seek preservation intact. Failed reads will discard the cache mapping because the backend may have changed both memory and position. The regression will compile the actual stdio sources and inject scribbling reads with zero or partial fd advance. The 4100-byte allocation and FILE ABI will stay unchanged.

The isolated source copy is still being prepared. The v1 patch, fixtures, receipts, and review are preserved under `read-error-fix/inputs`.

The fix retains the window’s capacity but clears its valid data and known position after a negative read. If `fread` already delivered bytes, it will return that confirmed prefix and set the error flag. It will not count bytes touched by the failed backend call or classify that failure as EOF.

The clean target build completed, and the focused fixture passes on the fixed source. Against the preserved v1 source, it reproduces wrong bytes after a scribbled refill, stale position after backend advance, and `EPERM` replacing the injected flush errno.

The tests also expose v1’s `freopen` cache leak. I’m finishing the raw failure records and the source, object, ABI, and artifact audits before writing the final paired receipt.

The recovery checks confirm the key difference: with v1, recovery after the failed read can return bytes for the wrong offset or report position 77 after a read intended to end at 40. The fix forces a descriptor seek and refill, returns the expected bytes, and reports position 40. The separate failed-seek tests still pass.

I’m also rebuilding a fresh, unmodified FS06 B locally so the final receipt covers a clean baseline/candidate pair.

Both clean builds are complete. All 224 baseline/fixed scenario executions pass under ASan/LSan/UBSan, and 36 expected failures from v1 are recorded separately. A persistent-error check also confirms that successful `fseek` cannot serve stale cached data while backend reads continue to fail.

I’m finishing the artifact audit and cost review. The requested allocation remains 4100 bytes per full target window, and the RV32 probe still reports a 132-byte FILE.

The object audit shows that only the three corrected stdio translation units differ from v1. The fix adds 38 bytes of kernel text; the complete candidate is 664 bytes above FS06 B, with data and BSS unchanged.

All 3343 objects in the fresh baseline match frozen B. FILE layout, configuration, workload objects, and AppFS checks pass. The remaining audit is the before/after check of protected files.

Implemented the isolated [read-error-fix revision](/home/regex/work/esp32s31-openvela/backups/xts-adaptation-and-test-evidence/korvo-fs-stdio-read-window/read-error-fix/README.md).

- Fixed all three blockers: failed-read cache invalidation, `freopen` window release, and public `fflush` errno handling. Failed-seek preservation remains intact.
- **224 passing scenarios** under ASan/LSan/UBSan. **36 reproduced v1 failures** remain separately recorded.
- Clean baseline/candidate builds passed; all **3343 baseline objects** reproduce frozen B.
- FILE remains **132 B**; window allocation remains **4100 B**. Kernel text is **+38 B versus v1**, with data/BSS unchanged.
- Frozen v1 and maintained trees remain unchanged.

The [final receipt](/home/regex/work/esp32s31-openvela/backups/xts-adaptation-and-test-evidence/korvo-fs-stdio-read-window/read-error-fix/final-receipt.json) identifies the matching kernel, AppFS and configuration hashes. Offline work only; no board operations or performance/xTS claims.
